strategyPosture: Stay with the rotation, not against it: hold existing exposure while leadership is narrow but credit is loose (HY 3.09%, SLOOS 0%), and do the research work on the DATA_AHEAD dislocations (AVGO, APP, NOW) rather than chasing the +25.67% 1-month momentum in PLTR into the October 14 CPI print.

themes.counterRead: The calm is real but narrow: leadership is rotating away from the index heavyweights and small caps are already in a downtrend, so index-level strength overstates the average stock. The rotation read holds only while credit stays loose — a SLOOS flip toward tightening would convert rotation into rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: Market concentration reads ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: the Mag7 average sits -9.33% from its 52-week high, a -8.93-point divergence gap versus SPY, with TSLA weakest at -23.3% and AAPL strongest at -2.5%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, well below the ~40% stress threshold). Breadth confirms the narrowness: IWM is -3.14% over 1 month and -6.24% over 3 months while QQQ is +5.88% over 1 month.
themes.label: Index Leadership Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY at 778.95, +0.65% on the day and only -0.4% from its 52-week high — so the market reads this as a healthy, broad tape.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS rising off 0% toward tightening territory, or the Mag7-vs-SPY divergence gap widening beyond -8.93 points while SPY itself breaks below its 52-week-high shelf.

themes.counterRead: Price is ahead of the rate data: stocks are discounting a soft landing that a 5.24% 10-year and 2.89% real yield do not confirm. The tight 3.09% HY spread says credit agrees with equities, which makes the pair vulnerable to the same CPI print rather than hedged against it.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 5.24%, the 30-year 5.6%, the 2-year 4.77% (2s10s +0.47), and the real 10-year is 2.89% — a restrictive real-rate regime. Yet high-yield spreads are only 3.09% and breakeven inflation is 2.35%, so credit is pricing no stress at all. The next two event risks are dated: CPI for September prints October 14 (HIGH signal strength, 5 hits) and the FOMC meets October 27-28 (HIGH, 6 hits).
themes.label: 5.24% 10Y, Tight Credit, Unbothered Equities
themes.narrative: Equities trade as if the rate backdrop is benign: SPY +2.79% over 1 month, VIX at 15.5, and buyers stepping into growth leaders like PLTR (+25.67% 1m) and META (+13.11% 1m).
themes.watchFor: September CPI on October 14 — a hot print that pushes the 10-year above 5.24% toward the 30-year's 5.6%, or HY spreads widening through 3.09%, breaks the calm-equities read.

themes.counterRead: This is where the data is ahead of price: revenue and cash flow are compounding while multiples compress on sentiment, the opposite of the index-level pattern. The risk is name-specific, not macro — a revenue deceleration at the next print would reclassify these from dislocation to deserved de-rating.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO trades at $361.54, -27% from its 52-week high, with revenue growing 55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M FCF (42.1% margin) — top conviction score 81, Tier A. APP is -62.5% from its high at $277.04 (RSI 35.4) with a 76% gross margin and 60.8% FCF margin. NOW is -27% from its high at $140.86 with revenue growing 23.1% YoY and a +7.4% 1-month trend already turning up.
themes.label: Dislocated Quality Growth: Fundamentals Ahead of Price
themes.narrative: The market has written off a cohort of growth names as broken stories — AVGO, APP and NOW all sit at FULL_SIGNAL dislocations flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, far below their highs while the index sits at its own high.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding above its current $361.54 dislocation with revenue growth staying near 55% YoY at the next report; APP RSI recovering off 35.4 without a new low below $277.04.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree inside the winners — generation and grid equipment are being paid for AI demand now — while the nuclear concept leg was narrative ahead of any data and is deflating on schedule. BWXT (-40.5% from high, revenue +18.3%, score 77 Tier B) is the one nuclear-adjacent name where the dislocation screen flags fundamentals ahead of price.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is a top-5 1-month leader at +10.47% (+4.04% today) and PWR is +13.22% over 1 month. The nuclear complex is the mirror image: SMR -30.85% over 1 month, URA -14.24% and OKLO -13.99%. VST itself is still -25.6% from its 52-week high (RSI 64.4), so the leaders are recovering, not extended.
themes.label: AI Power Splits: Grid and Generation Over Nuclear Concept Names
themes.narrative: The AI-power trade is treated as one theme, but the tape is splitting it in two: cash-generating power and grid names lead while pre-revenue nuclear names unwind.
themes.watchFor: SMR stabilizing after its -30.85% month or VST closing its -25.6% gap to the 52-week high — the first signals whether the split is done or still widening.
